justification: A dies on “at least ninety-two per cent of its sailings berth within ten minutes of the booked minute” — the payment turns on a proportion clearing a threshold, not on the average sailing’s lateness, and “within ten minutes of” is two-sided rather than “how far behind”. B dies on the two dates it straddles: “Since 2011 the operator has earned a quality payment” against “in 2016 the relief boat’s passenger certificate ran out and the company did not replace her” (Bexwarden also “drafted the punctuality clause … in 2011”). D dies on “A sailing that does not run is not late; it leaves the count altogether”, corroborated by the first quarter of 2023, when the crossing “lost forty-one sailings to weather and a gearbox, and its reliability figure was ninety-seven per cent, the highest it had ever been” — cancellation raises the figure, it does not dock the payment. Key C is arithmetically exact against “taken it in twenty-three of the last twenty-four quarters” (24 quarters = six years, one unpaid). No hedging or length tell: all four options are absolute and twelve words.

B dies on “Two boats and the old book gave you a departure every twenty-five minutes” — seventy is Cottam’s figure for the present one-boat service (“One boat gives you one every seventy”), so B inverts both halves. C dies on “Then there is work that really has got longer” together with the 2013 linkspan whose “locking sequence takes a manufacturer’s ninety seconds at each berth”: berth work is presented as longer now, not shorter then; and nothing says the 2005 book excluded loading — the round-trip figures imply a turnaround allowance existed. D dies on “The published reliability figure stood at seventy-one per cent in 2005”, a figure Cottam himself treats as a measurement (“the old seventy-one per cent measured a promise nobody could keep”), so measurement plainly predates the clause. Key A restates “The median crossing that year took twenty-four minutes against an eighteen-minute booking”.

A dies on “The book went from eighteen minutes to twenty-four in 2013, three years before the certificate ran out” — the passage pre-empts exactly this reversal. B dies on the cause the text actually assigns, “in 2016 the relief boat’s passenger certificate ran out and the company did not replace her”; the 2013 linkspan rebuild is a separate item never linked to the withdrawal. C dies on “the interval between departures went from twenty-five minutes to thirty-two” followed by “Some of the frequency was gone before the boat was”, which denies the word “first” outright. Key D is carried by the two intervals Cottam gives (25 → 32 from the book, 32 → 70 from losing the boat), so the boat removed the larger share of departures.

A dies on “Nobody disputes the stamps. Cottam has accepted the barrier series in writing, and does not contest the fifteen minutes” — the minutes are conceded by all parties, so the writer cannot think they show little. C is the near-key trap and still dies on “the stamps would bear either of the other two just as well”: the writer withholds the attribution itself, not merely its magnitude, and says “the timetable is the reading she prefers” — preferred, not shown. Her own “I’ll give you a range, not a number” is the bait, but that hedges size, whereas the writer’s sentence hedges the join. D dies twice, on “Nobody disputes the stamps” (her numbers are not doubted) and on “the stamps would bear either of the other two just as well” (the timetable is not granted). The four options fill the clean 2×2 grid of accept/doubt numbers × accept/reject cause, and B is not the only hedged option — C and D both hedge.

A dies because it states the contested causal claim as settled fact (“has kept its punctuality payment by lengthening the timetable”), against “Where Cattermay’s case thins is the join” and “the stamps would bear either of the other two just as well”; Bexwarden likewise “does not accept that it caused any of this”. It is Cattermay’s thesis, not the text’s frame. B has a verbatim-true first half but dies on its second: “Nobody disputes the stamps. Cottam has accepted the barrier series in writing” — there is no dispute over which number to believe, only over what connects them. C dies on “None of the three is arguing about the sentence Bexwarden raised herself” and on scope: the cancelled-sailings line is a closing thread of an eight-paragraph piece, explicitly marked as the one nobody contests. Key D matches both movements (71 → 96 per cent against 39 → 54 minutes) plus the three-way disagreement over the join.

A dies on “ett tilloppsdike ut mot myrens övre kant” together with “en vattningsränna går tvärs över sluttningen och faller nästan inte alls” — the ränna sits at the upper edge and runs along the contour, so it cannot be drawn through the middle feeding both sides. B dies on “Avvägningen gjordes med vattenpass och käppar, på de mindre anläggningarna efter ögonmått” — ögonmått is restricted to the smaller works, and Skrömtbäcken’s main ränna is given a measured gradient (“drygt en halv meter på fyrahundra”); the added “sedan vattnet hade släppts på” has no anchor at all. D dies on “Först då lämnade vattnet rännan längs hela dess längd i stället för att följa den till den lägsta punkten och skära sig ner där” — a single outlet is precisely the failure the rule exists to prevent. Key C restates “rännan skulle luta mindre än marken nedanför den” and is confirmed by the two gradients.

Four genuinely distinct, physically real processes, none of them nonsense: sediment/dissolved-nutrient fertilisation (A), oxygen-driven peat mineralisation (B, key), moisture as drought relief (C), and winter-ice frost insulation (D). A is the strongest temptation because it is the standard textbook mechanism of water meadows and the text concedes it operates elsewhere (“Längs de grumligare åarna i söder vägde slammet tyngre än här”) — right in the world, wrong here — but it dies on the sentence pair that names and excludes both of its halves: “Bäckvatten från myrmark är brunt och slamfattigt. Någon nämnvärd mängd mineraljord avlagrades inte på ängarna vid Skrömtbäcken, och halten av löst näring i vattnet var för låg för att ensam förklara skördeökningen.” C dies on “Det avgörande var syret” plus “Stillastående vatten gör tvärtom: det stänger ute luften” — wetness as such is presented as harmful and movement as the whole requirement (“hela den tiden skulle det röra sig”); the water is also “stängdes av ett par veckor före slåttern”, i.e. off before high summer. D is verbatim true as a proposition — P5 says the ice and snow “hindrade tjälen från att gå djupt, så att rötterna klarade sig bättre och tillväxten kom i gång tidigare på våren” — but it is not the huvudorsak the stem asks for: it is scoped to “På en del av markerna”, it belongs to autumn dämning rather than the sixty-day silning that defines the siläng, and the text attaches the stem’s own noun to the oxygen account alone (“för att ensam förklara skördeökningen” → “Det avgörande var syret”). Law 11 is satisfied because the passage designates a single main cause categorically rather than leaving the key merely ‘best’.

All three die on the agreement’s stated content, “fördelade vattnet i turer om fyra dygn och angav i vilken ordning turerna skulle tas”, which is also the key. A additionally lacks any anchor: maintenance appears only as “dämmet skadades av islossningen nästan varje vår”, with no allocation of responsibility. B is wrong on the object (vattnet, not myrhöet) and on the characterisation (a fixed order, not an uneven split). C exploits the adjacent “omkring niohundra dagsverken fördelade på tre somrar”, but the 1858 document allocates water, not digging days. The framing sentence “Till detta kom samordningen” confirms why the author raises it.

B dies on the two stated causal conclusions — “Hennes slutsats är att fodret upphörde att vara knappt” against “Orsaken söker han i arbetskraften, som drogs till sågverken och till Amerika” — so varför is exactly what divides them; timing is the evidence, not the quarrel. C dies on their different corpora: “har jämfört tidpunkterna i ett fyrtiotal socknar” against “har karterat rännsystemen i fyra socknar”, and each objects to the other’s material rather than to a shared reading of one body of evidence. D carries a verbatim-true premise (forty parishes against four) but its causal claim is false: the text roots Nolvide’s objection in selection, not size — “hennes socknar är valda bland dem som har bevarade dikningshandlingar” — and neither scholar raises sample size. Key A is carried by the pair of mutual source objections plus “kartorna sällan går att tidfästa närmare än ett par decennier” and the closing “ingen förde bok över hur många dagar som gick åt till rännorna”.

A dies on “samma jämna blå himmel över taken” — the sky is uniform; the bait, “Himlen ändras på varje kort”, says the sky is altered on every card relative to the plate, not that it differs between cards, and “samma” settles it in the adjacent sentence. C dies on “Nio plåtar har moln, och även på de korten ligger samma jämna blå himmel över taken” — the nine belong to the plåtar and the clouds are painted over on the cards. D dies on “På de flesta plåtarna är den en tom vit yta” plus “plåten kunde inte hålla himlen, alltså fick koloristen ge den en” — white is the plate’s state, and the card is exactly where a sky gets added. Three of the four are plåt/kort inversions, which is the unit’s core skill, and each is killed by an explicit adjacent clause.

A dies on the firm’s own production chain — “Fotograferingen skedde med glasplåt, tryckningen beställdes i Tyskland, och färgen lades på för hand i firmans lokal vid torget”, with “Fyrtioen plåtar finns kvar” — the plates are Vidbring’s own, and buying Vitthamn views from photographers in other towns is nowhere suggested. Noted fairly: A has the right logical shape in the world (bought-in stock images would indeed decouple postmark from exposure), so it is wrong per the text rather than wrong in itself. B dies on “Plåtarna kom till museet 1974, i två packlårar och utan förteckning” and on chronology: the card at issue is postmarked August 1919, inside the firm’s own 1904–1929 run, so no successor after publication ceased could account for it. C is the strongest survivor-candidate — it is true of the world, and “lagret” does appear in the passage — but it still dies on two explicit grounds. First, the stem asks about “när bilden togs”, and shelf time separates a postmark only from the printing, not from the exposure. Second, the passage glosses its own stock category with the reprint mechanism in the very next sentence, “Vidbring tryckte nya upplagor från samma plåt så länge ett motiv gick att sälja”, which is the key; no sentence puts printed cards in shops.
